gateProvenToFire.method: Wrote a two-occurrence mojibake file, `git add -N` so it entered `git ls-files`, ran the guard, then removed it.
gateProvenToFire.result: PROBE_SCAN_EXIT=1 with both hits reported by line and codepoint (U+00C2 U+00B7 and U+00E2 U+20AC).
gateProvenToFire.ratchetDivergenceTest: The baseline is a CEILING, so all three of its branches were exercised against the same 2-occurrence probe using temp copies of the script: ceiling 1 -> exit 1 (a file getting worse fails); ceiling 2 -> exit 0 silent (at ceiling); ceiling 3 -> exit 0 plus a NOTICE naming the file and telling the reader to lower the ceiling (a file getting cleaner never breaks the lane that cleaned it). Probe and temp copies deleted; clean re-scan confirmed exit 0.
gateProvenToFire.selfExemption: None. Every signature and sample in the guard is a \uXXXX escape, so the guard is scanned by its own rule. The first draft used literal samples and correctly flagged itself, which is DEV_PROCESS 2.6 earning its place again.

adversarialFindingsAgainstOwnWork.finding: The buildable row would have contradicted the declined-consume block.
adversarialFindingsAgainstOwnWork.checkedAtSource: Read mapBuildableDisplay in src/lib/buildable-display-vocab.ts rather than assuming. declined-consume returns cardState:'present' with cardLabel '0% — setbacks consume lot', so there is NO contradiction. The only absent buildable case is envelopeStatus==='declined'.
adversarialFindingsAgainstOwnWork.butFound: In that declined case the coverage block would have read 'buildable fills in from zoning setbacks for this parcel' beside the zoning and setbacks rows already saying exactly that — circular, and it inflates a one-cause gap into a three-item list.
adversarialFindingsAgainstOwnWork.fix: Coverage claims are now opt-in per row (FactRowSpec.inCoverageBlock). Exactly land use, zoning and setbacks claim coverage — the same three fields the retired bakedHasHonestAbsence used, so the SCOPE is unchanged and only the treatment moved. Derived rows (buildable) and identity rows (apn, county) render their state without claiming a coverage gap. Pinned by a test that asserts the set is exactly [landUse, setbacks, zoning].

adversarialFindingsAgainstOwnWork.finding: The provenance splitter could mangle a value whose description legitimately ends in parentheses, e.g. 'A1 — Vacant (rural)'.
adversarialFindingsAgainstOwnWork.fix: The trailing parenthetical must look like a machine key (hyphen/underscore/dot separated, or a middle-dot-joined list) to be split. A single plain word never matches. The failure mode is therefore a MISSED demotion, never a mangled fact. Both directions are pinned by tests.
adversarialFindingsAgainstOwnWork.residual: A source key that is a single bare lowercase word would not be demoted. Accepted: this shim is deleted when P-39 lands the typed split.

adversarialFindingsAgainstOwnWork.finding: The shim could double-split after P-39 lands a real provenance sibling.
adversarialFindingsAgainstOwnWork.fix: Splitting is opt-in per row via spec, and FactRow consumes a FactPresentation that already carries provenance as a separate field, so once the sheet supplies it the shim path is simply not taken.

adversarialFindingsAgainstOwnWork.finding: One pre-existing test broke, and it broke for the right reason.
adversarialFindingsAgainstOwnWork.detail: InspectCard.test.tsx asserted the card face contains 'Source: Bastrop County GIS'. Under I3 the provider key is exactly what must move behind the disclosure. The assertion was rewritten to pin the new contract (verification line and record date visible on the face, the provider key present only when the disclosure is open) rather than deleted. Recorded here because a broken assertion that is silently deleted is indistinguishable from a regression.
